authority.statement: This artifact records what each source actually establishes, including conflicts. Cross-model recurrence ranks experiments; it does not prove an exact 2005 4Runner byte layout, scale, unit, or ECU source.

evidence_classes.meaning: Toyota, Lexus, or SAE primary documentation. May establish diagnostic availability, procedure, applicability, or vehicle relationship, but not an undocumented raw broadcast-CAN layout.
Primary, reproducible vehicle research with a named vehicle, acquisition method, physical or diagnostic reference, or peer-reviewed analysis. Cross-model only unless the target configuration matches.
Version-pinned community DBC, logger definition, or listen-only notes. Useful for hypothesis ranking; never sufficient for promotion alone.

sources.scope: Toyota's owner manual for the 2005 4Runner identifies both 1GR-FE and 2UZ-FE engine configurations for the exact target model year.
proves: The unresolved target configuration can be either the 1GR-FE V6 or 2UZ-FE V8 family covered by the exact-model-year manual.
VIN and configuration resolution are mandatory before applying engine- or transmission-specific signal definitions.
does_not_prove: Any CAN identifier, payload layout, scale, unit, transmitting ECU, or diagnostic PID applicability.

sources.publisher: Toyota General 2005 Features content; archived on Scribd
sources.scope: Toyota-authored General 2005 Features CAN section comparing the 2005 4Runner, Tundra, and Sequoia networks.
proves: The documented 2005 4Runner/Tundra CAN network runs at 500 kbit/s.
The documented 2005 4Runner CAN connects the skid-control ECU, ECM, steering-angle sensor, yaw/deceleration sensor, and DLC3.
The 2005 Sequoia topology differs by adding suspension-control and translate ECUs, demonstrating option/model-specific network variation.
Toyota identifies repair manual publication 1165U for the 2005 4Runner CAN diagnostic procedure.
does_not_prove: Any raw broadcast-CAN identifier, payload layout, scale, unit, checksum, or exact ECU calibration.
That every target option or drivetrain has an identical traffic population.
sources.provenance_note: The archived pages identify Toyota copyright and Toyota figure/publication references, but the public host is an unversioned third-party mirror rather than an official Toyota endpoint. Claims are limited to the visible manual text.

sources.publisher: Toyota GSIC manual content; archived by ToyotaManuals on GitLab
sources.scope: Version-pinned archival copy of Toyota repair/new-features manual RM00T1U/NM0010U for adjacent-model-year 4Runner GRN210/GRN215 and UZN210/UZN215 configurations.
proves: The adjacent 4Runner generation exposes the steering-angle sensor through the intelligent tester CAN VIM and BUS CHECK workflow.
The same-generation manual distinguishes accelerator channels ACCEL POS and ACCEL POS#2 and publishes independent released/depressed voltage ranges.
The manual explicitly covers both GRN and UZN chassis families, reinforcing configuration-specific validation.
does_not_prove: That the 2005 target shares every 2006 calibration or option.
Any raw broadcast-CAN identifier, field position, scale, unit, checksum, or transmitter.
sources.provenance_note: The underlying content identifies itself as Toyota GSIC service information; the cited public host is a third-party archive, not an official Toyota publication endpoint.

sources.publisher: Toyota New Features manual content; archived by ToyotaManuals
sources.scope: Toyota Land Cruiser/Land Cruiser Prado New Features page describing the VSC CAN network and its participating nodes.
proves: The documented related-SUV VSC network runs CAN at 500 kbit/s.
The documented network connects the skid-control ECU, engine ECU, steering-angle sensor, yaw/deceleration sensor, DLC3, and an ECT ECU on the stated 1KD configuration.
does_not_prove: That the 2005 4Runner has the same node population, topology, CAN identifiers, payloads, or ECU calibrations.
sources.provenance_note: The PDF is Toyota-authored New Features content hosted by a third-party archival mirror.

sources.scope: Toyota states that Techstream Lite supports DLC3/J1962 diagnostic functions on 1996 and later Toyota, Lexus, and Scion vehicles marketed in North America.
proves: A factory diagnostic reference path exists for the target model year.
Techstream Data List values are suitable independent observables for synchronized validation.
does_not_prove: Any raw broadcast-CAN identifier, field layout, scale, unit, or checksum.

sources.scope: Toyota Tech Tip T-TT-0615-20 specifies a synchronized Techstream snapshot containing vehicle speed, engine speed, accelerator position, intake-air temperature, output-axis speed, NT sensor speed, selector status, lockup, and other drivability values.
proves: Toyota exposes independent reference values covering several current CAN hypotheses.
A marked, synchronized snapshot is an OEM-supported diagnostic workflow.
does_not_prove: That any listed diagnostic value is broadcast at a particular CAN identifier.

sources.scope: Toyota T-SB-0086-13 directs technicians to inspect the Techstream Steering Angle Sensor value on 2009-2011 Camry vehicles and publishes diagnostic ranges.
proves: Steering angle can be captured as an independent Toyota Data List reference on the Camry research lineage.
does_not_prove: The raw 0x025 scaling or its applicability to a 2005 4Runner.

sources.scope: The Lexus RX350/RX450h campaign procedure records Techstream accelerator sensor or accelerator-position Data List values at released and fully depressed states.
proves: Toyota/Lexus exposes independent accelerator-pedal references and distinguishes redundant sensor channels.
does_not_prove: That 0x2C1 uses the same encoding on RX, FJ Cruiser, Camry, or the target 4Runner.

sources.scope: Toyota T-SB-0160-18 directs technicians to compare engine speed and transmission revolution sensor NT speed in Techstream under a controlled Park condition.
proves: Engine and transmission input/turbine speed are distinct OEM diagnostic observables suitable for resolving the 0x2C4 versus 0x2D0 relationship.
does_not_prove: The identity or scale of 0x2D0 on the target vehicle.

sources.scope: Toyota identifies 4Runner, Land Cruiser Prado, LC200, and Lexus GX on a Tahara production line, and Prado and FJ Cruiser on a Hamura line.
proves: Those vehicles are defensible related-SUV research cohorts rather than arbitrary Toyota comparisons.
does_not_prove: Shared ECUs, software, network topology, CAN identifiers, or signal layouts across model years.

sources.scope: Toyota identifies the FJ Cruiser as a 1GR-FE 4.0-liter, five-speed electronically controlled, part-time-4WD vehicle.
proves: The FJ mapping is a more relevant powertrain research lead for a VIN-confirmed 1GR-FE 4Runner than an unrelated Toyota passenger car mapping.
does_not_prove: That the target 4Runner is 1GR-FE or that the FJ CAN mapping is identical.

sources.scope: Primary 2010 Camry research correlating physical vehicle actions with 11-bit, 500 kbit/s CAN traffic.
proves: 0x025 behaved as steering data, 0x2C1 as accelerator/throttle-pedal data, 0x2C4 as engine speed, and 0x224 as brake-pressure data on the tested Camry.
0x022 was steering-like; 0x023 and 0x223 were observed but unresolved; 0x2D0 was observed but unresolved.
does_not_prove: Exact 2005 4Runner field scaling, layout, direction, unit, or applicability.

sources.scope: Peer-reviewed transmitter-fingerprinting analysis using 2010 Camry CAN data and a separate ground-truth method.
proves: 0x223 and 0x224 originated from the same ECU on the tested Camry.
0x2C1 and 0x2C4 originated from distinct transmitters on the tested Camry.
does_not_prove: Payload semantics, target-vehicle ECU identity, or field scaling.

sources.scope: Primary 2010 Lexus IS250 experiment using synchronized crank/cam and pedal/brake measurements, DLC CAN logging, controlled driving, and EDR replay to identify RPM-related messages.
proves: 0x2C4 byte position 1 carried engine-RPM-related data on the tested Lexus.
0x2C1 byte position 7 tracked accelerator-pedal-voltage behavior on the tested Lexus.
0x2D0 carried RPM-related data and a current-gear field on the tested Lexus.
does_not_prove: The exact 2005 4Runner scale, payload layout, unit, or applicability.
That the FJ turbine-speed transform applies to 0x2D0 on the target.
That the Lexus current-gear field and FJ selector field occupy the same byte.
sources.provenance_note: The EVU article identifies the 2016 congress paper and authors; the cited ResearchGate copy exposes the experimental tables and methods used in this lineage review.

sources.scope: Primary Prius acquisition project with preserved CAN logs, VSI-2534 acquisition, and VBox GPS used to validate vehicle speed.
proves: A synchronized external reference and preserved raw logs can validate Toyota CAN hypotheses reproducibly.
does_not_prove: Any current 2005 4Runner hypothesis without a matching, reviewed identifier and field.

sources.scope: Version-pinned Toyota DBC corpus covering iQ, Prius, and generated DBC families used by later Toyota and Lexus platforms.
proves: 0x025 steering-angle definitions recur, but the 2009 iQ definition is signed 11-bit at 1 degree/count while Prius and generated Toyota definitions are signed 12-bit at 1.5 degrees/count.
A byte-6 accelerator field at 0.5 percent/count recurs in a generated Toyota ADAS definition.
does_not_prove: An exact 2005 4Runner DBC or a single universal Toyota layout.

sources.scope: Community mapping labeled for a 2012 FJ Cruiser.
proves: A related-SUV community artifact maps 0x2C4 to engine RPM, 0x2C1 to accelerator position, 0x2D0 to turbine speed and selector state, 0x025 to steering, 0x223 to brake state, and 0x224 to pressure-like data.
does_not_prove: Exact target applicability, correctness, or universality across FJ/4Runner/Prado/GX.

sources.scope: Community transcription labeled as an AiM generic Toyota/Lexus protocol.
proves: The corpus contains 0x025, 0x224, 0x2C1, and 0x2C4 definitions, including 0x2C4 at 0.78125 rpm/count.
does_not_prove: Vehicle years, exact supported models, target applicability, or universal field positions.

sources.scope: Community transcription labeled as an AiM Toyota Auris protocol.
proves: The artifact maps 0x2C4 at 0.78125 rpm/count and 0x2C1 byte 6 at 0.5 percent/count, and also defines 0x0B0/0x0B2 wheel speeds and 0x224 brake pressure.
does_not_prove: Auris model year, exact target applicability, or correctness of physical scaling.

sources.scope: Community transcription labeled as an AiM Lexus IS F protocol.
proves: The artifact maps 0x2C4 at 0.78125 rpm/count and 0x2C1 byte 6 at 0.5 percent/count, while supplying different 0x224 pressure scaling and a different 0x2C4 air-temperature transform than the FJ mapping.
does_not_prove: Exact target applicability or which conflicting transform is correct for the 4Runner.

sources.scope: Explicitly listen-only Toyota Yaris notes whose author labels fields as guessed.
proves: The author observed 0x2C4 first-word behavior consistent with high-rate engine revolutions and recorded 0x0B0/0x0B2 wheel-speed candidates and a 0x224 brake bit.
does_not_prove: Engineering-unit scales, Yaris model year, or target applicability.

vehicle_line_matrix.usable_conclusion: The exact-model-year manuals confirm both 1GR-FE and 2UZ-FE configurations plus a 500 kbit/s VSC CAN joining the ECM, skid-control ECU, steering-angle sensor, yaw/deceleration sensor, and DLC3. No authoritative public exact-target raw payload definition was found; all production signal definitions remain blocked.

The adjacent 4Runner manual and Prado New Features manual establish relevant diagnostic channels and a 500 kbit/s related-SUV topology. The FJ is a rational high-priority source when the target is VIN-confirmed 1GR-FE. None of those relationships proves raw CAN identity.

These sources support physical correlation, transmitter grouping, and external-reference methodology. The Camry and Lexus experiments directly corroborate several target identifiers while remaining cross-model evidence.
Repeated identifiers reveal Toyota message-family lineage, while the conflicting width, placement, scale, and units demonstrate why model-specific validation is mandatory.

The pinned opendbc platform catalog shows broad reuse of a small set of generated Toyota DBC families in later vehicles. It does not include an exact 2005 4Runner definition and must not be back-applied blindly.

signal_lineage.candidate: engine speed in the first 16 payload bits
signal_lineage.agreement: All seven cross-model artifacts associate 0x2C4 with engine-speed behavior; the FJ and three pinned AiM-derived files use 0.78125 rpm/count, while the physical Lexus study independently confirms the RPM-related identifier and first byte position.
conflicts: An IS F community definition applies a 2.5*raw-40 intake-air-temperature transform where the FJ community file labels the same candidate byte as raw degrees Celsius.
No authoritative source establishes the exact target scale or target byte semantics.
signal_lineage.target_decision: Highest-priority candidate; display only as unverified engineering data until synchronized J1979 PID 0x0C or Techstream comparison passes.

signal_lineage.agreement: The Camry experiment identifies pedal behavior; the physical Lexus experiment independently identifies one-indexed byte 7; FJ, generated Toyota, Auris, and IS F artifacts place a 0.5 percent/count candidate at zero-indexed byte 6.
conflicts: The generic Toyota/Lexus community DBC places a seven-bit pedal field elsewhere at 1 percent/count.
Other Toyota generations use different accelerator messages and normalized units.
signal_lineage.target_decision: High-priority candidate; require rest plus separated pedal levels against Techstream or supported J1979 accelerator position.

signal_lineage.agreement: The identifier repeatedly belongs to a steering-angle family.
conflicts: Pinned definitions disagree between signed 11-bit at 1 degree/count, signed 12-bit at 1.5 degrees/count, and an FJ circular-angle formula equivalent to approximately -0.087890625 degree/count.
Direction, center offset, and valid range are unresolved on the target.
signal_lineage.target_decision: Semantic family is strong; no degree value is allowed until center/left/right Techstream correlation resolves width, scale, direction, and offset.

signal_lineage.agreement: Every relevant source associates 0x224 with braking, a brake bit, or pressure-like data.
conflicts: Field positions and scales differ materially across Camry/FJ, generic Toyota/Lexus, Auris, IS F, and Yaris artifacts.
The retained target candidate field was not exercised and remained static in the audited sample.
signal_lineage.target_decision: Do not display pressure units. First prove a repeated brake-press response and compare it with a Toyota Data List pressure or stop-light observable.

signal_lineage.agreement: The FJ artifact proposes a brake-state meaning, and Camry primary research proves 0x223 and 0x224 shared a transmitter on that test vehicle.
conflicts: The CSU semantic study left 0x223 unknown, and transmitter grouping is not semantic proof.
signal_lineage.target_decision: Keep as a brake-family experiment candidate, not an accepted stop-light switch.

signal_lineage.candidate: transmission turbine/input speed and selector code
signal_lineage.agreement: The FJ artifact supplies the turbine/selector hypothesis, the physical Lexus study independently finds RPM-related and current-gear data in 0x2D0, and Toyota documents an independent NT-speed reference workflow.
conflicts: The CSU Camry study observed 0x2D0 but did not identify it.
Only the FJ raw-CAN source supplies the turbine layout and 0.390625 rpm/count scale.

The Lexus paper places current gear in its fifth byte position, while the FJ artifact places a selector candidate in its third byte position; indexing conventions aside, the layouts conflict and must not be merged.
signal_lineage.target_decision: Weak-to-moderate candidate; resolve only with synchronized engine speed, NT/turbine speed, vehicle speed, selector, and shift-state data.

signal_lineage.agreement: The target and Camry both contain the identifier; the Camry experiment described steering-like behavior.
conflicts: No second independent field mapping or exact semantic source was found.

signal_lineage.agreement: Both target and Camry evidence contain a seven-byte 0x023 message.
conflicts: The Camry research left it unknown.
A pinned opendbc 0x023 definition is for an aftermarket Zorro steering sensor and is explicitly not evidence for the OEM target frame.

signal_lineage.agreement: No reviewed source established a relevant mapping.

verification_sequence: Resolve VIN, engine, drivetrain, market, and option configuration.
Run read-only SAE J1979 supported-PID enumeration before requesting standardized values.
Capture Techstream or a trusted scan-tool reference on the same monotonic timeline as passive CAN.
Validate 0x2C4 engine speed first, then 0x2C1 accelerator, 0x025 steering, 0x224/0x223 braking, and 0x2D0 turbine/selector.
Preserve competing transforms and rejection evidence; never choose a transform solely because it looks plausible.
Promote only through a versioned signal definition, golden replay, and missing/stale/range tests.
